The case is moving through the court system with Harrell's appearance scheduled for this week, though additional details about the incident and charges have not yet been released publicly.

item.content:encoded:
Escambia County animal control responded to a call on a local resident's property where a red fox had become severely entangled in netting, according to the Escambia County Department of Animal Welfare.

The department's team worked to safely free the trapped fox from the netting, which can pose serious risks to wildlife when left unattended. The incident highlights the dangers that discarded or improperly secured netting can create for local fauna.

Escambia County residents who encounter trapped or injured wildlife are encouraged to contact animal control rather than attempting rescue themselves, which can put both people and animals at risk.

The rally-style fundraiser leveraged the court setting to create an engaging atmosphere for supporters. Organizers are expected to make Rally On the Court an annual event, building on the momentum from this first year. For families in Okaloosa County and surrounding areas seeking resources related to childhood cancer support, the event represents a growing local network dedicated to the issue.

item.title: New personalized melanoma vaccine offers hope for cancer patients
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: A Baldwin County oncologist says a promising new vaccine being tested could transform how doctors treat melanoma by creating personalized treatments tailored to individual patients' cancers. Dr. Jan Kemnade, an oncologist with Infirmary Health, told WKRG News 5 that the experimental vaccine represents a significant shift toward personalized…
item.content:encoded:
A Baldwin County oncologist says a promising new vaccine being tested could transform how doctors treat melanoma by creating personalized treatments tailored to individual patients' cancers.

Dr. Jan Kemnade, an oncologist with Infirmary Health, told WKRG News 5 that the experimental vaccine represents a significant shift toward personalized medicine in cancer care. Rather than using a one-size-fits-all approach, the vaccine would be custom-built to target the specific cancer cells in each patient.

"This vaccine really shows what personalized medicine is all about," Kemnade said, highlighting how the treatment could potentially prevent melanoma from returning after initial treatment.

The vaccine is currently in testing phases, and if successful, could offer melanoma patients a new weapon in their fight against the disease. Experts say the approach could eventually extend beyond melanoma to other cancer types.

item.title: Daphne Opens Expanded Justice Center With New Municipal Courtroom
item.dc:creator: newsroom

The upgraded facility includes a brand-new courtroom designed to accommodate more cases and participants while incorporating modern security features and courtroom technology. The…
item.content:encoded:
Daphne's municipal court is back in operation at the city's newly expanded Justice Center after nearly two years of renovation work on the multi-million dollar project. The upgraded facility includes a brand-new courtroom designed to accommodate more cases and participants while incorporating modern security features and courtroom technology.

The expansion represents a significant investment in the city's judicial infrastructure, addressing space constraints that had plagued the previous courthouse setup. According to WKRG News 5, the new courtroom is equipped with enhanced security measures and contemporary audio-visual systems to support proceedings.

The project's completion marks the end of a lengthy construction period during which court operations were relocated elsewhere in the community. City officials have emphasized that the upgraded Justice Center will improve efficiency in handling municipal cases and provide better working conditions for judges, court staff, and the public.

The Pensacola Interstate Fair is one of Northwest Florida's largest annual events, drawing thousands of visitors each year to the fairgrounds in Pensacola.

The event has grown since its first year, establishing itself as a popular October tradition for families looking to get hands-on with machinery and equipment they don't often encounter in everyday life. Details on specific dates and times are expected to be announced soon.

item.title: Atlantic disturbance could develop into tropical depression this week
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The National Hurricane Center is monitoring a subtropical Atlantic disturbance that has the potential to become a tropical depression in the coming days, according to WKRG News 5. While the system remains in the open Atlantic, residents and businesses across the Gulf Coast should keep tabs on the National Hurricane Center's updates as the system…
item.content:encoded:
The National Hurricane Center is monitoring a subtropical Atlantic disturbance that has the potential to become a tropical depression in the coming days, according to WKRG News 5.

While the system remains in the open Atlantic, residents and businesses across the Gulf Coast should keep tabs on the National Hurricane Center's updates as the system develops. Even disturbances that don't immediately threaten land can shift course or intensify rapidly during Atlantic storm season.

The weather service will issue routine updates on the disturbance's position and development potential. Pensacola-area residents can monitor the latest forecasts through the National Weather Service office in Mobile or the National Hurricane Center's website for any changes that could affect Northwest Florida.

item.title: Free car seat safety checks offered in Bay Minette
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The Bay Minette Fire Department and North Baldwin Infirmary are joining forces to provide free car seat safety inspections for families in the area. The program aims to ensure children and infants are properly secured during vehicle travel, addressing a critical public safety concern that affects young passengers across Baldwin County and the…
item.content:encoded:
The Bay Minette Fire Department and North Baldwin Infirmary are joining forces to provide free car seat safety inspections for families in the area. The program aims to ensure children and infants are properly secured during vehicle travel, addressing a critical public safety concern that affects young passengers across Baldwin County and the surrounding region.

According to WKRG News 5, certified technicians will be available to check car seats for proper installation and correct usage, helping parents identify potential safety issues before they become dangerous. Improper car seat installation remains a leading cause of injury and death among young children in traffic accidents.

This type of community partnership has proven effective in other areas, combining emergency services expertise with healthcare resources to reach families who might not otherwise have access to professional safety guidance. Residents interested in participating can contact the Bay Minette Fire Department or North Baldwin Infirmary for scheduling details and specific dates for the safety checks.
